title: Form renderer: "a defaultValues reset is not a user edit" holds only for callers who do NOT memoize the callback
body:
Filed unassigned per Prime Directive #10. Surfaced while wiring `FormSchema.onChange` for #4259, and deliberately not addressed there — see "Why this is not part of that card" below.

## What happens

`packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` places its value subscriptions in **layout** effects, on purpose, so that a `defaultValues` reset (a record landing in edit mode) is not reported to the host as if the user had edited every field the record filled. The comment above the `onAction` subscription states the mechanism precisely: React runs every layout DESTROY before any layout CREATE, so a caller passing a fresh callback each render "has this subscription torn down before the reset runs and re-established after."

The load-bearing words are **"a fresh callback each render."** The guarantee is delivered by the callback's *identity changing*, which is what forces the effect to re-run and therefore to unsubscribe across the reset. A caller who wraps the same callback in `React.useCallback` — normally a pure performance optimization — keeps a stable identity, the effect never re-runs, the subscription stays live through the reset, and the reset **is** delivered.

## Measured

Against `origin/main` + the #4259 wiring, a host passing `onChange` and `onDirtyChange` through `React.useCallback(..., [])`, then committing a new `defaultValues` (the edit-mode record landing):

```
onChange calls after the reset:      [ { name: 'Loaded', note: 'from server' } ]
onDirtyChange calls after the reset: [ false, false ]
```

With the same host passing inline arrows instead, `onChange` receives nothing for the reset. Same component, same data, same code path — the only difference is whether the caller memoized.

Note `onDirtyChange` is **correct in both cases**: it reports `false`, because the renderer calls it explicitly after the reset with a computed dirtiness rather than relying on the subscription ordering. So the file already contains the shape that does not depend on caller identity; the subscription-ordering channels are the ones that do.

## Why it matters

- Memoizing a callback is supposed to be semantically neutral. Here it silently flips a behavioural guarantee, in the direction that produces a false "the user edited this" signal — the exact failure #2968 was filed about.
- It is invisible at the call site: nothing in the type, the docs or the renderer says "do not memoize this callback."
- It is identity-dependent, so it will reproduce intermittently across consumers depending on unrelated refactors.

## Scope: which channels

- `onAction` (`type: 'form_change'`) — pre-existing, unchanged by #4259.
- `onChange` — inherits the same property as of #4259, because the ruling there was explicitly to reuse this plumbing.

## Why this is not part of that card

The maintainer ruling on #4259 was to wire `onChange` "using the same subscription plumbing `onDirtyChange` proves exists in the file". Changing the ordering mechanism would change `onAction` behaviour as well, which is pinned by other tests, and picking the correct semantics is a design question rather than a mechanical fix: it is genuinely arguable whether a value-change channel *should* report a programmatic reset (for `onChange`, "the values changed" is arguably true; for an action typed `form_change` it is more clearly meant as a user edit). That fork needs deciding, not guessing, so #4259 pinned only the inline-arrow case its ruling described and left this one open. #4259 is not addressed by this issue and remains a separate concern.

## Possible exits (not decided here)

- Make it identity-independent the way `onDirtyChange` already is — drive the notification explicitly around the reset instead of relying on subscribe/unsubscribe ordering.
- Or accept it and document the constraint on the declared callbacks.

## Reachability

Any consumer that memoizes a `onChange` / `onAction` callback on a form that also receives `defaultValues` asynchronously (every edit-mode form that fetches its record). No in-repo caller currently does both, which is why this reads as latent rather than a live break.
